v: A reader that lacks a successor can see its predecessor as current. It cannot count records it does not know exist. The laws promise convergence, not freshness.
A reader must not see half a changeset. The planned place closes each changeset through atomic rename. Readers ignore a partial last line.
Content order breaks ties by claimed times, so a skewed clock picks a fork's winner. Every head of a fork is still shown.
Fold laws do not check signatures or standing. They require an admitted record set in which each id names one record.
"Since" means segments not yet seen, not an offset, or a late segment is missed.
